result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever the rest of the name is. This covers a plain `mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock(old)`, `mock-größe` and `mock模拟`. The `Scoping*` tests in `codeanalyzer` pass. I didn't add test cases for the new folder names, and I didn't run the other cases you listed.

I changed the two mock rules in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around lines 393–394). The old pattern allowed only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and spaces, and needed at least one character after `mock`. The new patterns are `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`, so the match stays inside one folder name.

- **Folders that must stay test code:** they all still match. `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` start with `mock` or `__mock`.
- **Backslash paths:** these are covered without further changes, because `SourceFileFilter.matches` also tries the path with `\` turned into `/`.
- **Not matched:** `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match, since the pattern needs `/mock` at the start of a folder name. `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are files, and the pattern requires a trailing `/`.
